input.summary: The owner asks whether overlapping completion-time ranges and p=0.6 from a descriptive pilot are sufficient to label the paper claim disproven. They are not: this pilot is descriptive-only, and neither distribution overlap nor a non-significant p-value establishes no effect, equivalence, or disconfirmation. A separately reviewed inferential design is required before any claim label can be assigned. This response returns the packet as-is with clarifying questions about the unresolved design gaps needed for any future inferential follow-up.
clarification_questions: What estimand and equivalence margin (if any) would you want a future inferential design to target — e.g., mean difference in flow completion time in milliseconds, with a pre-specified margin for practical equivalence?
What source data or software fixture (with a verifiable SHA-256) would supply the TCP flow completion time observations for an independent check or new measurement?
What resource budget (wall-clock seconds, maximum observations, and estimated cost) are you willing to allocate for a follow-on inferential pilot?

proposal.problem: The packet describes a synthetic claim that adding 20 ms emulated delay changes TCP flow completion time, but no inputs, configurations, metrics, or protocol details were provided in the saved packet.
proposal.question: Can overlapping observed completion-time ranges and a p-value of 0.6 from a descriptive pilot be used to label the paper claim disproven?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two emulated conditions are implied: a baseline (no added delay) and a treatment (20 ms added delay), under a fixed bottleneck. Exact bottleneck parameters, topology, and TCP variant are unspecified in the saved packet.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is a synthetic networking paper claim provided for development evaluation; no full text or prior empirical results are available for comparison.
proposal.alternatives: The observed overlap in completion-time ranges could reflect insufficient sample size, high within-condition variance, measurement noise, or a genuinely small effect — none of these alternatives can be distinguished from the current descriptive output alone.
proposal.design: This is a descriptive pilot only. No inferential estimand, sampling model, dependence structure, decision criterion, or equivalence margin has been specified or reviewed, so no claim label can be assigned from the current results.
proposal.metrics: TCP flow completion time (units unspecified in packet). No bounds, decision thresholds, or equivalence margins are defined.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck rate, TCP variant, flow size, and number of replications are all unspecified in the saved packet and must be resolved before any controlled comparison can be interpreted.
proposal.inputs: No input files, software fixtures, or verifiable SHA-256 hashes were provided in the saved packet; source and context hashes are synthetic placeholders.
proposal.limitations: Overlapping observed ranges and a non-significant p-value do not establish no effect or equivalence under the server's descriptive-only policy. An inferential conclusion requires a separately reviewed design specifying the estimand, sampling and dependence structure, decision criteria, and any justified equivalence margin.
